extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal Title IX requirements (elementary/secondary schools, postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and institutional legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for institutions on conducting Title IX grievance procedures under §106.45, including investigation standards, evidence handling, parties' access to evidence, privacy/FERPA interactions, and related procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction of information not relevant to the allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may redact information that is not relevant to the allegations of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When redacting, the recipient must ensure full compliance with obligations under §106.45 and, if applicable, §106.46. See discussions of §§106.6(e), 106.45(b)(5) and (f)(4), and 106.46(e)(6). Recipients must also take reasonable steps to protect privacy (§106.45(b)(5)) and to prevent and address unauthorized disclosure (§§106.45(f)(4)(iii) and 106.46(e)(6)(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: FERPA disclosure for school officials with legitimate educational interest
rubrics_metrics.description: FERPA permits disclosure of personally identifiable information from a student's education record without prior written consent if disclosure is to a school official determined to have a legitimate educational interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply criteria set forth in the institution's annual FERPA notification of rights. See 20 U.S.C. 1232g(b)(1)(A); 34 CFR 99.7(a)(3)(iii), 99.31(a)(1)(i)(A). FERPA does not relieve a recipient of the obligation to gather sufficient evidence under §106.45(f)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation requirement (§106.45(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide for adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation of complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision lays the foundation for equitable adjudications and requires equitable treatment of complainants and respondents. §106.45(b)(1) requires grievance procedures to treat parties equitably; §106.45(b)(2) requires that any person designated as a Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual party. The Department will offer technical assistance and guidance as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative burden on recipient (§106.45(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient, and not the parties, bears the burden to conduct an investigation that gathers sufficient evidence to make a determination whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department substituted 'burden . . . to conduct an investigation' for legalistic phrases but the meaning is the same as prior requirements: do not shift burden to complainants or respondents. Recipients may not use consent policies to require a respondent to prove consent. FERPA considerations do not relieve the recipient of this obligation; see related discussions of §§106.6(e), 106.45(e), (f)(4), and 106.46(e)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to present fact witnesses and other evidence that are relevant and not otherwise impermissible (§106.45(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide an equal opportunity for the parties to present fact witnesses and other inculpatory and exculpatory evidence that are relevant and not otherwise impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevance is defined in §106.2 and the relevance threshold limits unnecessary or harmful introduction of irrelevant testimony or evidence. §106.45(b)(7)'s prohibition on impermissible evidence applies regardless of relevance. The Department declined to categorically allow or disallow character evidence; character evidence must be relevant. The recipient has discretion to allow expert witnesses (moved to §106.46(e)(4) for certain postsecondary cases), but any decision to allow experts must be applied equally to the parties. §106.45(g) and §106.45(h)(1) provide processes for questioning witnesses and evaluating evidence persuasiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and determination of relevance (§106.45(f)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must review all evidence gathered throughout the investigation and assess that evidence for relevance and impermissibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may make relevance determinations during the investigation but remain responsible for assessing relevance in light of all evidence gathered. To avoid excluding relevant evidence, a recipient may need to revisit earlier relevance determinations and reconsider previously excluded witnesses or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to access relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence or an accurate description (§106.45(f)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide each party with an equal opportunity to access the evidence that is relevant to the allegations and not otherwise impermissible either by (a) providing access to the relevant evidence ('evidence option') or (b) providing an accurate description of such evidence ('description option').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the recipient initially chooses the description option and then any party requests access to the evidence, the recipient must provide all parties equal opportunity to access the underlying evidence. The recipient may choose either option but must ensure equal opportunity across parties and equal mode of delivery subject to auxiliary aids and disability or language accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and sufficiency of a description of the evidence (§106.45(f)(4)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient provides a description of the evidence, that description must be 'accurate'—it must fairly summarize the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence and be sufficient to provide the parties with a reasonable opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy means the description must allow parties a reasonable opportunity to prepare arguments, contest relevance, and present additional evidence. The Department declined to prescribe specific contents beyond accuracy and sufficiency. Oral descriptions are permitted but must be documented (e.g., audio) to satisfy recordkeeping (§106.8(f)(1)). A recipient may nevertheless choose to provide the underlying evidence in all cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable opportunity to respond to evidence or description (§106.45(f)(4)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must be given a reasonable opportunity to respond to the evidence or to the accurate description of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonableness depends on the nature and volume of evidence and may vary by case; generally the opportunity occurs at the end of the investigation after evidence is gathered, but recipients may permit response at other points. Recipients must ensure parties can meaningfully respond in line with due process principles (see Goss). The Department declined to provide fixed examples of reasonableness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing and addressing unauthorized disclosures (§106.45(f)(4)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must take reasonable steps to prevent and address parties' unauthorized disclosure of information provided under §106.45(f)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorized disclosures can chill reporting, threaten privacy, and impair fairness. The Department does not prescribe specific steps because what is reasonable will vary; options include informing parties of expectations and consequences, or using software to restrict distribution. Privacy protections in these final regulations and FERPA may limit disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal treatment in mode and extent of access to evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide all parties with the same description of the evidence or the same access to the underlying evidence and must ensure equal opportunity as to the mode of delivery (e.g., physical or electronic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may not give one party access to underlying evidence while providing only a description to another party. However, equal opportunity does not require identical accommodations where auxiliary aids or language services are necessary to ensure effective communication for a specific party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and recordkeeping for grievance procedures (§106.8(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must maintain records documenting the grievance procedures for each complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(f)(1) does not specify written records only; if a recipient uses an oral description of evidence, it must document that description (e.g., audio recording) to comply with recordkeeping requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion to tailor procedures to circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have discretion to tailor the manner of providing access to evidence (description or underlying evidence), considering nature of complaint, age of parties, severity of alleged conduct, volume of evidence, and other case-specific or recipient-specific factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description option may be more appropriate for younger students and less severe consequences; high school, postsecondary, or expulsion cases are more likely to warrant access to underlying evidence. Recipients must nevertheless articulate consistent principles in their grievance procedures for deciding when to provide description versus evidence (§106.45(b)(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: No mandatory written investigative report under §106.45(f)(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike §106.46(e)(6), §106.45(f)(4) does not require access to a written investigative report or require that a written investigative report be prepared for all §106.45 cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient that chooses the description option under §106.45(f)(4) may, but is not required to, provide the description in the form of a written investigative report. Recipients choosing to provide a description must still meet the accuracy and sufficiency requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert witnesses not required; discretionary use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department is not requiring recipients to allow expert witnesses in §106.45 cases; the provision regarding expert witnesses was moved to §106.46(e)(4) for certain postsecondary harassment cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient may allow expert witnesses as part of investigating and resolving complaints under §106.45, provided the decision to allow experts is applied equally to the parties. The Department cited concerns that experts may introduce delays without meaningful benefit in cases governed by §106.45.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character evidence handled by relevance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to categorically allow or disallow character evidence; character evidence must meet the 'relevant' definition in §106.2 to be admissible or considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(f)(2) requires parties have opportunity to present relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence, and §106.45(b)(6) requires recipients to objectively evaluate such evidence. The relevance requirement will exclude character evidence that will not aid the decisionmaker in determining whether sex discrimination occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'relevant' evidence and limits on sexual history disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations use an expansive definition of 'relevant' (see §106.2) to mean evidence related to the allegations of sex discrimination, but final regulations prohibit disclosing evidence of a complainant's sexual interests and prior sexual conduct except as narrowly permitted by §106.45(b)(7)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The combined approach—expansive 'relevant' definition plus prohibition on disclosing sexual history except narrowly—addresses concerns about overbroad discretion. For further explanation see discussions of §§106.2 and 106.46(e)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and absence of conflicts or biases for designated personnel (§106.45(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person designated as a Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker must not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to add a separate paragraph about impartiality because §106.45(f) and §106.45(b)(2) already address impartial investigations and personnel neutrality. This requirement supports equitable adjudications and fair outcomes.
